<ExternalIntegrationProducts name={"Raspberry Shake"} products={[{"label":"Raspberry Shake","href":"https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Raspberry+Shake&tag=gladproj-20"}]} />

Your [Raspberry Shake](https://raspberryshake.org) personal seismograph in Gladys: the vibration level
of the ground at home, minute by minute, shaking detection with its peak and its duration, and the
online status of the station. Works with every Shake model (1D, 3D, 4D, RS&BOOM).

Two sources, used together:

- the **UDP output** of the Shake (Datacast), sent straight to Gladys on your local network: the live
  samples, from which Gladys computes the vibration level (RSAM), the peak and an STA/LTA trigger;
- the **public data** of the Raspberry Shake network (AM), when your Shake shares its data: whether the
  station is still sending, even without the UDP output.

It is not an early warning system: a home seismograph also feels footsteps, doors, washing machines and
trucks, and the detection says that the ground moved, not that an earthquake happened. For the
earthquakes reported by seismologists near your home, see the EMSC Earthquakes integration.

Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome. The analysis was tested on a real recording of a
public station (the magnitude 3.7 Pyrenees earthquake of 3 August 2026, 5 km from station AM.R6881),
replayed in the UDP format of the Shake; no physical Shake was connected. Not affiliated with Raspberry
Shake, S.A.

## What you get

- A **Raspberry Shake** device per station: online status and last data received; with the UDP output,
  vibration level (RSAM, counts), peak amplitude (counts) and shaking detected, with their history.
- A **dashboard widget**: station status, live vibration level and peak, and the vibration level of the
  last day as a chart.
- Three **scene triggers**: shaking detected, back to calm (with the peak and the duration), station
  offline.
- A **Check the station now** action in the configuration screen.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.2 or later (the integration publishes a UDP port through a sub-container).
- A Raspberry Shake on the same network as Gladys, for the UDP output.
- Internet access from the Gladys host for the online status (`data.raspberryshake.org`, HTTPS).

## Configuration

### Station and UDP output

1. Find the code of your station: on the web page of your Shake (`http://rs.local`, or its address),
   or on the [station map](https://stationview.raspberryshake.org). It looks like `R1A2B` (network
   `AM`).
2. In Gladys, Integrations → Raspberry Shake → Configuration, type the code and save.
3. The top of the configuration screen shows the address and the UDP port Gladys chose for the
   integration (for example `192.168.1.20`, port `40123`). On the web page of the Shake, open Settings →
   **Datacast**, add this address as target host and this port as target port, then save and restart
   the data producer as the Shake asks.
4. Create the device in the **Discover** tab.

The Shake sends its samples about four times a second per channel: a few kilobytes per second on your
local network. The port is chosen by Gladys and kept: the Shake only needs to be set once. If your
Shake gets its address from your router, a fixed address (DHCP reservation) lets you fill **Address of
the Shake**: packets from any other device are then ignored.

### Settings

| Setting               | Default | Meaning                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Station code          | empty   | `R1A2B` or `AM.R1A2B`, any case.                                            |
| Use the UDP output    | on      | Off: online status and last data only, from the public data of the network. |
| Address of the Shake  | empty   | Optional IPv4 address: UDP packets from any other address are ignored.      |
| Shaking detection     | Normal  | STA/LTA ratio that starts a detection: low 6, normal 4, high 3.             |
| Offline after         | 1 hour  | Time without data before the station is offline (1, 2 or 6 hours).          |
| Language of the texts | French  | Names of the features (at their creation) and dates.                        |

## Device

| Feature                | Type             | Meaning                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Station online         | binary           | Data received in time: UDP in the last 2 minutes, or recent public data. |
| Last data              | text             | Date and time of the last data received (updated every 10 minutes).      |
| Vibration level (RSAM) | number, counts   | Mean absolute amplitude over each minute, offset removed.                |
| Peak amplitude         | number, counts   | Largest absolute amplitude over each minute.                             |
| Shaking detected       | vibration sensor | 1 from the trigger until 10 seconds of calm.                             |

The last three need the UDP output. Values are in **counts**, the raw unit of the Shake: compare them
with your own station's usual level (the station of the recording read about 900 counts before the M3.7
earthquake, 5 km away, which peaked at 1.16 million). The vertical geophone (EHZ) is used, else the
first seismic channel received; the infrasound channel of a Boom is ignored.

The **detection** compares the mean amplitude over 1 second with the mean over 30 seconds (STA/LTA),
the classic trigger of seismology: it starts at the chosen ratio and ends after 10 seconds below 1.5
(2 in low sensitivity). The long term average needs 30 seconds of data after a start or a gap.

## Dashboard widget

Add the **Raspberry Shake** widget to a dashboard: name of the station, live vibration level and peak,
a 24-hour chart of the vibration level (can be hidden in the widget settings), and a status block
(online, last data, ground calm or shaking, UDP packets in the last minute). Without the UDP output,
only the status block is shown.

## Scene triggers

- **Shaking detected**: the trigger went on. Variables: the station code and the STA/LTA ratio.
- **Back to calm**: the shaking is over. Variables: the station, the peak amplitude (counts) and the
  duration (seconds). Use the peak to tell a footstep from an earthquake in a scene condition.
- **Station offline**: the station was online and no data came within the configured delay. Variables:
  the station and the date of the last data.

The **Shaking detected** device feature can also be used as a regular device trigger.

## Scene examples

- When **Back to calm** fires, if the peak is above your usual level by a large margin, send yourself a
  message with the peak and the duration.
- When **Station offline** fires, send a message: the Shake may have lost its power or its network.
- Every evening, read the vibration level of the day on the chart to see the traffic, the wind and the
  activity of the house.

## Data sources, terms and quotas

- UDP output: the samples never leave your local network; nothing is stored, the analysis runs in
  memory.
- Public data: the FDSN web services of Raspberry Shake (`https://data.raspberryshake.org/fdsnws/`),
  free and without account, for stations that share their data. The integration reads only the
  headers of a few kilobytes of data every 10 minutes (a short window, then narrow probes further back
  when the station is silent). The archive lags about 30 minutes behind real time, hence the one-hour
  minimum before offline. Citation of the network: Raspberry Shake, S.A. (2016), Raspberry Shake
  [Data set], International Federation of Digital Seismograph Networks,
  https://doi.org/10.7914/SN/AM.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No UDP data from the Shake"**: check the Datacast target (the address and the port shown in the
  configuration screen, not port 8888), that the data producer was restarted, and that no firewall on
  the Gladys host blocks incoming UDP. With an address of the Shake set, check it: the logs say once
  which address was ignored.
- **"Station is not on the Raspberry Shake network"**: the code is wrong, or the Shake does not share
  its data. The UDP output still works.
- **Many detections**: footsteps and doors near the Shake trigger at high sensitivity: choose normal or
  low, or move the Shake to the floor of a quiet room.
- **The Configuration screen shows `{{port:shake_udp}}`**: the receiver has not started yet; reload the
  page after a few seconds.
- Logs: Integrations → Raspberry Shake → Supervision; `LOG_LEVEL=debug` shows every minute and every
  detection.

## Limits

- One station per Gladys. The counts are not converted into ground velocity, and no magnitude is
  computed: a home seismograph cannot locate an earthquake on its own.
- The detection is a simple STA/LTA trigger on one channel, without any filter: it says that the ground
  shook near the Shake, whatever the cause.
- The online status without UDP needs a station that shares its data on the network, and arrives
  about 30 minutes late.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Raspberry Shake asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connect your Raspberry Shake | `section` | No | Type the code of your station below. For live data, open the web page of your Shake (rs.local), Settings, Datacast, and add the target host \{\{gladys_host\}\}, port \{\{port:shake_udp\}\} (chosen by Gladys). Without it, only the online status is followed, through the public data of the network. |
| Station code | `string` | Yes | Shown on the web page of your Shake and on the station map, e.g. R1A2B. |
| Use the UDP output | `boolean` | No | Vibration level, peak and shaking detection, computed in Gladys from the live samples. |
| Address of the Shake (optional) | `string` | No | When set, UDP packets from any other address are ignored. |
| Shaking detection | `select` | No | STA/LTA trigger ratio: high also catches footsteps and doors near the Shake. |
| Offline after | `select` | No | Without UDP, the public data of the network arrives about 30 minutes late. |
| Language of the names and texts | `select` | No | Feature names (set when the device is added) and dates. |

## How to install Raspberry Shake in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Raspberry Shake appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-raspberry-shake:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-raspberry-shake](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-raspberry-shake).

Raspberry Shake requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
